thread:
sasha: heads up — during the canary for release/optim/12 the az-gpu nodepool went into quarantine and gitops blocked reconcile. seeing helm hook timeouts on the post-upgrade job. anyone around?

infra-bot: [ALERT] gitops-sync: cluster=prod-eu-west-3 namespace=redwood-inference status=QUARANTINED resource=helmrelease/az-gpu-pool reason=hookTimeout

jon: can you paste the helm hook logs? might be a job stuck on PV resize or waiting for kubelet.

sasha: pasted. short log: 
```
kubectl -n infra logs job/az-gpu-preflight-1234
2026-03-17T09:42:01Z Starting nodecheck
2026-03-17T09:42:12Z Checking GCE quotas... OK
2026-03-17T09:43:35Z Waiting for kubectl drain to complete: pod/allocator-backfill-xyz still terminating
2026-03-17T09:45:00Z Hook timeout exceeded (2m)
```

maya: that drain timeout sounds like pods on spot nodes refusing eviction (preemption-protection?). we've seen kube-proxy CNI hang with long cordon/drain before.

ryan: terraform drift detector also flagged pool_size on az-gpu-prod as 3 vs desired 5 — looks like autoscaler was prevented from adding nodes because the helm hook held the pool in a pending state.

jen: cost note — if we scale prod to 5 for manual remediation we'll burn ~12 GPU-hours at $X/hr. ok for now?

jon: quick triage steps I'd do now: 1) kubectl describe node/affected for kubelet events 2) check pod stuck reason 3) if it’s safe, force delete stuck pods with --grace-period=0, then re-run helm reconcile.

sasha: ran describe. truncated: 
```
Name: gpu-node-3
Conditions: Ready=False (Reason: NetworkUnavailable)
Events:
  09:40:12  kubelet  NodeHasSufficientMemory  NoSchedule  kubelet has insufficient free memory
  09:42:05  kubelet  EvictionThresholdMet  Pods evicted due to ephemeral-storage
```

maya: ephemeral-storage evictions explain pods stuck terminating. those pods mount local scratch; drain waits for graceful stop. safe to force-delete if replacement can reschedule.

ryan: terraform plan snippet shows the desired node_count=5 but provider shows current=3. drift detected at 2026-03-17T09:30:00. autoscaler was set to disabled=true in the HelmRelease because of the earlier incident.

sasha: options: A) patch helmrelease to increase hook timeout and re-trigger helm job B) temporarily unquarantine via gitops override and let autoscaler scale to desired size C) manual node add via cloud console and then let gitops reconcile.

jen: prefer B for minimal code change: override quarantine -> let autoscaler scale -> then fix root cause in staging. cost is acceptable for short window. :+1:

jon: if we unquarantine we need a rollback plan. add a gitops flag in the repo with a short TTL and audit note. also we should annotate the HelmRelease with `reconcile.kubernetes.io/force=true` after fix.

sasha: I'm going to open a tiny PR to infra-configs that sets gitops/quarantine=false for az-gpu-prod with a comment. will include links to the incident and timeline.

sasha: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra-configs/pulls/382 — description: temporarily clear quarantine to allow autoscaler rebound; will revert after scaling verified.

infra-bot: [CI] PR 382: lint OK, plan shows patch to HelmRelease.az-gpu-prod: quarantine=true -> false.

maya: while we wait on approval, can someone craft a k8s command to force-delete the stuck pods if scale doesn't happen in 10m?

jon: command: 
```bash
kubectl -n workloads get pods -o wide | grep Terminating | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r kubectl -n workloads delete pod --force --grace-period=0
```

ryan: once nodes come up, let's run a quick smoke: sample inference job plus tiny perf check to make sure KV-cache warm paths are okay. I'll handle that.

jen: tagging cost owner @finance for post-mortem.

sasha: PR merged. unquarantine applied. autoscaler observed new node creation at 09:55. scale to 5 completed by 09:58. pods rescheduled.

maya: confirmed, no more terminating pods. helm hook job retried and finished. gitops synced and cleared QUARANTINED state.

jon: followups: 1) increase hook timeout to 5m in chart to account for heavy eviction cases 2) add an env-check to the preflight job to skip cordon/drain delay when ephemeral-storage pressure present 3) add an alert for autoscaler-disabled=true in prod.

sasha: noted. creating issues: infra#210 (hook timeout bump), infra#211 (preflight skip logic), infra#212 (autoscaler-disabled alert).

ryan: nice. closing loop: ordering action items and tagging owners. thanks team. :rocket:
